title: Ambiguity
body:
Natural language carries more than one reading of the same sentence, and the readings can
differ in what follows from them. Removing that ambiguity is most of what translating into
symbols achieves.

**Lexical ambiguity** is one word with several meanings.

```
"The bank was steep."          the side of a river
"The bank was closed."         the financial institution
```

**Structural ambiguity** is one arrangement of words with several grammatical readings.

```
"Visiting relatives can be boring."
    the relatives who visit are boring
    the act of visiting them is boring
```

An argument can equivocate by using one word in two senses across its premises, which makes it
look valid while connecting nothing. A formal language has exactly one reading per
[[Well-Formed Formula]], so the ambiguity has to be resolved during translation, before
any reasoning starts.
